name: Darkspear tribe
summary: Across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, the Darkspear tribe follows Thrall’s Horde. Driven from Stranglethorn Vale and rescued from a sea witch in the Great Sea, the jungle trolls follow Shadow Hunter Vol’jin from Sen’jin Village. They now struggle to reclaim the Echo Isles from Zalazane.

sections.title: Exile and Salvation
sections.body:
Once part of the broken Gurubashi Empire in Stranglethorn Vale, the Darkspear were smaller and less ruthless than their neighbors. For centuries, they endured famine and fought the brutal Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter tribes. Driven out to sea, they settled on remote islands, where murlocs, Kul Tiran sailors, and a naga sea witch threatened them.

Their elder chieftain, Sen’jin, was captured and slain in dark rites beneath the sea. Before he died, he foretold that the orc Warchief Thrall would lead the Darkspear to a new destiny. Thrall’s fleet rescued the survivors. They pledged loyalty to the new Horde and sailed west to Kalimdor.

sections.title: The Fall of the Echo Isles
sections.body:
After reaching Durotar, the Darkspear made their home on the tropical Echo Isles, just off the mainland coast. Admiral Daelin Proudmoore’s fleet drove them into the swamps of Dustwallow Marsh for a time. Horde forces then destroyed the invaders.

Witch doctor Zalazane embraced twisted voodoo and seized control of his kin’s minds. To preserve his free people, Vol’jin, Sen’jin’s son and successor, ordered another evacuation. The Darkspear now live in coastal Sen’jin Village. Champions cross the water to slay Zalazane and free their thrall-bound brothers.

sections.title: Voodoo and the New Horde
sections.body:
The Darkspear have adapted quickly to the Horde’s values of honor, unlike their cannibalistic jungle kin. They have enclaves in Malaka’jin in the Stonetalon Mountains, Shadowprey Village in Desolace, and Zoram’gar Outpost in Ashenvale. In Orgrimmar, they make their spiritual home in the Valley of Spirits, where shadow hunters and witch doctors commune with the loa.

Their scouts, bat riders, and powerful hexes are respected. Yet old traditions run deep, and some ancient rites their allies frown upon are still practiced quietly in the dark.

faq.q: Why are the Darkspear trolls in the Horde?
faq.answer: During the Third War, Warchief Thrall’s fleet took shelter on the Darkspear islands during a violent storm. A naga sea witch and her murloc minions captured the trolls and orcs, but Thrall freed them. Chieftain Sen’jin died in the escape after foreseeing that Thrall would guide the Darkspear to safety. In gratitude, Sen’jin’s son Vol’jin swore the tribe’s allegiance to the Horde.

faq.q: Who leads the Darkspear tribe right now?
faq.answer: Vol’jin leads the Darkspear tribe. He is the son of the fallen chieftain Sen’jin, a cunning shadow hunter, and one of Warchief Thrall’s closest and most trusted confidants. Vol’jin advises the Horde from Orgrimmar’s Valley of Spirits and oversees the struggle to reclaim the Echo Isles.

faq.q: Why do the Darkspear live in Sen'jin Village instead of the Echo Isles?
faq.answer: The Darkspear live in Sen’jin Village because witch doctor Zalazane betrayed them on the Echo Isles. He used dark magic to enslave the minds of his fellow trolls. Rather than slaughter their enchanted kin, Vol’jin ordered the free Darkspear to retreat to the mainland shore and founded Sen’jin Village as a base for their fight.

faq.q: Where did the Darkspear originally come from?
faq.answer: The Darkspear came from the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale, where they belonged to the fractured Gurubashi Empire. Smaller and less merciless than rivals such as the Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter, they suffered constant warfare and starvation until they were driven out of the Eastern Kingdoms.

faq.q: Do Darkspear trolls still practice cannibalism?
faq.answer: Officially, the Darkspear have renounced cannibalism and headhunting as tribal policy so they can live in harmony with Thrall’s Horde and honor their alliance. Centuries of jungle heritage run deep, and whispers persist that darker traditional rites are still observed in secret, far from prying eyes.

faq.q: What deities do the Darkspear worship?
faq.answer: The Darkspear revere the loa, powerful primal spirits and animal gods. Their faith centers on a vast pantheon, honored through the voodoo rites of their witch doctors and shadow hunters.

angles.text: As a Darkspear troll, you carry the weight of an exiled people rebuilding on foreign shores. Every blow you strike against Zalazane on the Echo Isles or your brutal Gurubashi cousins in Stranglethorn Vale helps secure your tribe’s survival.

The bond between orc and troll was forged in the blood of the Third War. Thrall considers Vol’jin his closest brother-in-arms, and Darkspear scouts and witch doctors serve faithfully beside Durotar’s warrior clans.
From bat riders defending the skies to herbalists brewing draughts in Stonetalon, the Darkspear bring mystical cunning and stealth to the Horde’s raw martial might.

As a shaman, you can see how Darkspear shamans join the ancient worship of primal loa spirits with elemental teachings learned from their orc and tauren allies. Je’neu Sancrea represents the tribe within the Earthen Ring.
